newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Dec 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Dec 31.

text.p: Former Speaker of the House Peter Tapsell, doyen of rugby writers Terry McLean, High Court Judge Tom Thorp and retired Massey University scientist Ella Campbell are the New Year knights and dame. The four became Knights Companion and Dame Companion of the New Zealand Order of Merit. Page 1.

As dawn breaks over the North Island today, the worst weather brought by Cyclone Fergus should be heading out to the Pacific Ocean, meteorologists said last night. Early damage reports show the worst-hit part of the North Island was Coromandel and the Kaimai Ranges, with galeforce winds and torrential down-pours sending campers heading home. Page 1.

Police and the Maritime Safety Authority are investigating whether criminal charges will be laid in the wake of the boating collision that claimed the lives of five members of the same family at Wellington Harbour's entrance on Sunday night. At 10.40 p.m. on a calm clear night, the 17-metre fishing boat Maria Luisa was flipped after a collision near Barett Reef with the container ship Sydney Express as the ship was leaving Wellington Harbour. Page 1.

The Tukituki MP, Labour's Rick Barker, yesterday welcomed plans for New Zealand Vietnam War veterans to get an official welcome home parade, 23 years after the last soldiers were pulled out of the conflict. Planning has started for New Zealand's first full parade of Vietnam veterans, some of whom were smuggled back into the country in civilian clothes to avoid anti-war protests. Page 2.

A state of emergency was declared by Civil Defence on the Coromandel Peninsula late yesterday. Thames district civil defence controller Basil Morrison said heavy rain and strong winds left by tropical cyclone Fergus had left the peninsula all but cut off by flooding and slips. Page 2.

Listed apple grower Grocorp Pacific has taken a swipe at the Apple and Pear Board over low returns and the decision to refuse Grocorp's application to export a large part of its own crop. Auckland-based Grocorp is one of the biggest suppliers of export apples to the Apple and Pear Board. Grocorp's criticism of the board follows the long-running attacks by South Island firm Apple Fields on the board's protected status as the prime pipfruit exporter. Page 13.

The buyer of 2.2 million shares in listed investment fund Direct Capital Partners is a mystery but market sources say the cash-rich company is ripe for share raiding. The off-market buy at 73 cents on Friday pushed the share price up to 77 cents by close of trade yesterday. The net tangible asset backing of the company's shares is about 90 cents. Page 13.

Malaysia's Malex Industries is talking with Brierley Investments about several construction joint ventures in Asia. "We are negotiating on several mega-projects," Arul Manickman, a director of Malex, said yesterday. "We want to use the expertise of James Hardie." He did not elaborate. BIL owns 26.7 percent of James Hardie Industries, an Australian building materials company and has indicated it wanted to raise its stake. Page 13.

News that Coles Myer chief executive Peter Bartels received a more than $A1 million boost to his pay packet brought executive salaries under the spotlight in 1996, but Bartels was not alone in being handed a bonus that the average person could retire on. A survey in the Australian Financial Review found that in 16 of the Top 40 Australian companies the average chief executive pay packet had grown by about 57 percent in the past five years.

Insurance giant AMP has sold a trademark building on the corner of Auckland's Queen and Victoria Street for $8.3 million. The buyer's name was not disclosed, but was described as "a local family trust" by estate agent Barfoot and Thompson which undertook the deal.

Malex Industries says it is involved in talks with Brierley Investments about several construction joint ventures in Asia. "We are negotiating on several mega-projects," said Arul Manickam, a director of Malex.

Thousands of washed out holidaymakers remained stranded by flood waters early today as Cyclone Fergus triggered a state of emergency on the Coromandel Peninsula before homing in on the Eastern Bay of Plenty. Their isolation was highlighted at 12:45 a.m. on Tuesday when the Westpac rescue helicopter took off from Auckland to try to fly through heavy cloud to rescue a man suffering heart problems in the Coromandel settlement of Whangapoua.

For once the familiar, slightly mischievous T.P. McLean smile was replaced by a more serious aspect. After all, being our first sports reporter to be knighted brought a certain solemnity to the life of Sir Terry McLean, Knight Companion of the New Zealand Order of Merit. Sir Terry is one of three new knights and a dame named in the New Year honours list.

Cyclone Fergus is forecast to run out of puff over New Zealand this morning, leaving either havoc in its wake or a few red faces at the MetService in Wellington. After issuing warnings on Sunday that Fergus would hit Cape Reinga at noon yesterday and tear a path of destruction down the middle of the North Island, the Wellington-based weather forecasters appeared to be covering their bets yesterday.
